blocks.title: High Availability, Sites, and Diversity comparison
High Availability, Sites, and Diversity exam shortcuts
items: Traffic spread across servers → LOAD BALANCING
The goal is distributing requests or workloads.
Example: A load balancer sends users to healthy web servers.
Systems operate as a group → CLUSTERING
The systems coordinate to provide service or failover.
Example: A database cluster continues after one node fails.
Need fastest alternate site → HOT SITE
The site is already equipped and ready.
Example: Recovery staff can switch operations quickly.
The site has partial infrastructure but needs configuration or data restoration.
Example: Hardware exists but current data must be loaded.
Cheapest site, slowest recovery → COLD SITE
The location exists but technology must be installed or configured.
Example: Space and power are available, but servers are not.
Regional disaster must not affect both sites → GEOGRAPHIC DISPERSION
Place redundant sites far enough apart to avoid the same event.
Example: Primary and backup data centers are in different regions.
blocks.example: Focus on recovery speed, continuity, redundancy, data loss tolerance, and site or power requirements.

questions.q: A company distributes incoming web requests across several healthy servers. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Load balancing spreads traffic or workload across multiple systems.

questions.q: Several database nodes operate together and one can take over if another fails. Which concept best fits?
questions.explanation: Clustering groups systems so they work together and can provide failover.

questions.q: A disaster recovery location is fully equipped with current systems and can be activated quickly. Which site type is this?
questions.explanation: A hot site is ready to operate with minimal setup.

questions.q: A recovery site has hardware installed but requires configuration and current data before use. Which site type is this?
questions.explanation: A warm site is partially ready and requires some setup.

questions.q: A recovery location provides space and power, but equipment must still be installed. Which site type is this?
questions.explanation: A cold site has basic facilities but little ready-to-run technology.

questions.q: Primary and backup data centers are placed in distant regions so one natural disaster is unlikely to affect both. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Geographic dispersion reduces shared regional risk.

questions.q: An organization intentionally uses different operating systems for redundant systems to reduce a common vulnerability affecting both. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Platform diversity reduces common-mode failures by avoiding identical technology stacks.

questions.q: An organization distributes workloads across two different cloud providers. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Multi-cloud uses more than one cloud provider.
